architecture.mechanism: Controlled overprotection at coating defect sites using calcareous deposit formation to reduce effective holiday area and current demand
architecture.intervention: Temporarily raise rectifier output to -0.95 V_CSE to trigger rapid calcareous-scale deposition over the largest coating holidays, then back off to maintain -0.85 V at remote test stations; the calcareous layer shrinks the bare-metal exposed area without reducing current available downstream
architecture.expected_effect: Reduced anodic current drain per kilometer so that the far-end potentials shift from -0.72 V toward the −0.85 V criterion while total rectifier amperage stays within its fixed budget
architecture.falsification_test: Install a reference cell adjacent to the largest known coating defect and monitor for 7 days after a step-up to −0.95 V; if the local potential holds at or below −0.95 V with no measurable drop in pipe current despite the increased voltage, the calcareous-deposit mechanism is not engaging and the overprotection strategy must be rejected
